diagrams.title: From Threat to Priority: The Risk Chain
diagrams.subtitle: Follow the path: a threat meets a vulnerability, risk is estimated, then scored and prioritized.

nodes.label: Threat
nodes.detail: Actor or capability that can cause harm. Its activity is informed by threat feeds and internal or external intelligence.
nodes.exam: A threat exists even if no vulnerability is exploitable yet.

nodes.label: Vulnerability
nodes.detail: Weakness in a system, process, or control. It becomes a concrete risk when a threat can exploit it.
nodes.exam: Do not confuse vulnerability (weakness) with threat (what exploits it).

nodes.label: Risk
nodes.detail: Risk = vulnerability × threat. Likelihood depends on exposure and exploitability; impact depends on asset criticality.
nodes.exam: A critical flaw on an isolated test bench may be less risky than an exposed medium flaw.

nodes.label: CVSS
nodes.detail: Common Vulnerability Scoring System: severity calculated using base, temporal, and environmental metrics.

nodes.label: CVE
nodes.detail: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures provides a public identifier (CVE-2024-xxxx). CWE, on the other hand, classifies the type of code weakness.
nodes.exam: CVE = enumeration; CWE = weakness; CVSS = score. Three distinct concepts.

nodes.label: Context
nodes.detail: Expands the score: Internet exposure, existence of a public exploit, asset criticality, compensating controls.
nodes.exam: CVSS environmental metrics capture part of this context.

nodes.label: Prioritization
nodes.detail: Mitigate, accept, transfer, or avoid the risk. Treatment is followed by verification (re-scan).
nodes.exam: Risk acceptance must be documented and reassessed.

nodes.label: Verification
nodes.detail: After remediation, verify that the flaw is no longer exploitable and close the ticket.
nodes.exam: Without verification, the vulnerability management loop is not closed.

quiz.question: Which concept measures the severity of a vulnerability on a scale of 0 to 10?
